headline: Trump's Energy Ceasefire Is a Post the Plants Have Not Joined
deck: Trump posted an immediate Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire. Zelenskyy called it news to him as a Kyiv plant and Kharkiv's TES No 5 were struck after the post.
body: President Donald Trump of the United States said: "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" the Guardian reported. [E3] NPR reported that his brief social media post said only that the ceasefire took effect immediately, adding: "Do not break it!" [E4] The BBC reported that the US president insisted it was "effective immediately" but provided no details. [E2]
Moscow has yet to comment, the BBC reported. [E1]

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the deal to stop long-range attacks was "news to me", the Irish Times reporting the announcement was apparently without consulting him. [E5] The BBC reported he said it was "news" to him that an energy truce was in effect. [E6]
He told the Axios website, the Guardian reported: "If President Trump negotiated it with Putin – please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready and we will accept it." [E7]

Zelenskyy, the BBC reported, said Ukraine is ready not to strike at Russian energy and counts on Russia's similar readiness and on the agreement of the president of the United States of America on this, and that his officials look forward to clear details of America's dialogue with Russia; the Ukrainian presidency reported Ukraine was ready to stop striking Russian energy infrastructure on a reciprocal basis. [E6][E10]
Kyiv would support it if Moscow did, the BBC reported. [E8]

Zelenskyy wrote on social media late on October 11: "This is good news for everyone -- and it is important that it become reality," Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported, and NPR reported he said his country "welcomed" the announcement by Trump as "good news for everyone". [E9][E13]

Zelenskyy later said Russia had hit a power plant in Kyiv with a drone, causing power cuts, followed by strikes on energy facilities in the north-eastern Kharkiv region. "All of this happened after the president of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire," he said. [E11] Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported he said Russia launched an Iran-style shahed drone "at a power plant in Kyiv, and there were power outages in many areas." [E9]

The Guardian reported that the Ukrainian president said the Russians hit thermal power station No 5 in the eastern city of Kharkiv, the latest of more than 200 strikes this week against electricity generation and transmission facilities in Ukraine. Remaining output at the station has not been published. [E12]
In an evening address he said, "Unfortunately, Ukrainian skies have been infested with Russian 'shaheds' all day today," NPR reported, referring to drones launched by Moscow. [E13]
Despite the announcement, Russian overnight strikes hit multiple Ukrainian power plants, Zelenskyy said, the Irish Times reported. [E14]

**The desk's reading.** Trump's energy ceasefire is a post the plants have not joined. Kyiv is treating it as conditional: ready to stop striking Russian energy if Moscow does the same, and still asking when the halt begins. After the post, Zelenskyy reported a drone on a Kyiv power plant, TES No 5 in Kharkiv, shaheds through the day, and overnight hits on multiple Ukrainian plants. Moscow has not confirmed a halt. The competing reading is that Trump's announcement plus Kyiv's willingness already constitutes the agreement, and the strikes were munitions launched before the post. That reading needs a named site going quiet and a Russian confirmation. Since this paper's 11 October diesel-loading forecast, the new physical record is named Ukrainian plants still in the strike log after the post.

**The next test.** A halt at named energy sites, with Moscow confirming it, would show the post had reached the plants. Further strikes on TES No 5, the Kyiv plant or another named energy site, or continued Moscow silence while those sites stay in the strike log, would show it had not. Review at 15:00 UTC.
